title: Trail and Summit
premise: When a flood delivers a sealed chest bearing the crest of Kestria—a nation erased from maps forty years ago—to Edmund Vane's mountain hut, he discovers it holds the inheritance claim of a family he never knew he had, and the last living proof that Kestria's royal line survived. Pursued by a collector's mercenaries who want the chest destroyed and shadowed by Ilse, a Kestrian archivist who needs it to restore her people's legal identity, Edmund must guide them across the Serpent Range before the dry season ends and the passes close. Betrayal, avalanche, and the truth of who betrayed Kestria force Edmund to choose between the anonymity he has guarded for twelve years and the belonging he never believed he deserved. He reaches the summit pass as the first snow falls, delivers the chest to the Kestrian council, and finally stops counting miles—choosing to stay and build a life among the people he once carried on his back.
about_author: Coral Halloran is a former alpine rescue volunteer who writes adventure fiction from a farmhouse at the foot of the northern ranges, where she keeps meticulous trail journals that feed her novels. Trail and Summit is her fourth book and the first in a loosely connected series about people the wilderness refuses to let go.

chapters.title: The River's Offer
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Twelve years after his blacklisting, Edmund drags a waterlogged chest from a flooded river near his high hut. The seal of dead Kestria stares up at him. He wants to burn it; instead he pries one corner open and finds a birth record bearing his mother's name. Beat: restless solitude cracked open by fate.

chapters.title: What the Chest Remembers
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Inside: documents proving a Kestrian heir survived the annexation, a locket, and a map of the Serpent Range marked in his father's handwriting. Edmund realizes the father who abandoned him was Kestria's royal cartographer. Beat: grief and fury entwined; the past refuses to stay buried.

chapters.title: A Stranger on the Switchbacks
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Ilse Brenner, Kestrian archivist, climbs toward Edmund's hut with mercenaries two days behind her. She has traced the chest for a decade. When she finds Edmund alive—his face on old Kestrian records—she nearly weeps. Beat: hope arriving exhausted and desperate.

chapters.title: Terms of Passage
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Ilse explains the chest can restore Kestrians' legal existence before a tribunal that convenes when the dry season ends. Edmund refuses; his blacklisting means capture at any border. She offers the one thing he can't dismiss: proof of who informed on his father. Beat: pride wrestling with hunger for truth.

chapters.title: Two Days Behind
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. The collector's enforcer Voss interrogates a village postmaster, closing in on the hut. He wants the chest burned because a restored Kestria would invalidate his employer's land empire. Beat: cold menace; the clock starts ticking.

chapters.title: The Hut Burns
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Mercenaries torch Edmund's hut while he and Ilse scout the trailhead. Twelve years of measured, contained life go up in smoke. Edmund saves only the chest and his father's map. Beat: rage transmuted into resolve—no going back.

chapters.title: Company of Strays
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. In the valley town of Ferrow they gather a party: Doss, a disgraced ferryman who owes Edmund a life-debt; Maret, a teenage runaway who can read the old Kestrian script. A found family assembles without anyone admitting it. Beat: wary warmth.

chapters.title: The First Pass
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. The party crosses the low Serpent saddle ahead of schedule. Edmund's old mastery returns; the mountains speak to him again. Maret catches him smiling and won't let him live it down. Beat: rediscovered joy shadowed by Voss's distant signal fires.

chapters.title: Border Ghosts
chapters.summary: Doss's POV. At a checkpoint, Doss's forged papers nearly fail. Edmund walks in openly under his blacklisted name to draw the guards—and is recognized, beaten, and released with a warning. Beat: the cost of his past made flesh; Ilse sees his scars for the first time.

chapters.title: Night of the Locket
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Ilse opens the locket: a portrait of Edmund's mother, Kestria's last queen's lady-in-waiting, holding an infant. Ilse tells Edmund he is the heir the documents protect. He throws the locket into the fire; Maret retrieves it. Beat: inheritance as burden, not gift.

chapters.title: Voss Closes the Gap
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Voss bribes a range warden and learns the party's route. He splits his mercenaries to trap them at the Ironbridge gorge. Beat: tightening noose; Voss's own history as an annexation orphan hinted at.

chapters.title: Ironbridge
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Ambushed at the gorge, the party crosses a rotting rope bridge under fire. Doss cuts it behind them with Voss's lieutenant still on it, a choice that haunts him. Beat: survival bought with a stain on the soul.

chapters.title: The Shepherd's Valley
chapters.summary: Maret's POV. A hidden valley of Kestrian descendants takes them in—people who still sing the old songs but deny the old name out of fear. Maret, who never had a people, is dazzled. Beat: belonging glimpsed, and its price of fear made visible.

chapters.title: The Elder's Refusal
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. The valley elder refuses to let the chest pass through, fearing reprisal. Ilse argues until dawn; the elder yields one guide, her grandson Tam, and a warning: the high passes are lying about the weather. Beat: persuasion, division, and grudging alliance.

chapters.title: Weather That Lies
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Edmund reads the sky and knows the dry season is ending early. He pushes the party hard; Maret's feet blister; tempers fray. Doss accuses Edmund of chasing his father's ghost at their expense. Beat: leadership under strain; the mountain as antagonist.

chapters.title: The Frozen Chapel
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Sheltering in an abandoned Kestrian chapel, they find frescoes of the coronation—and the face of the man who betrayed the royal line to the annexation forces. Ilse goes pale: he is the ancestor of the tribunal's chief justice. Beat: revelation that the system itself is the enemy's legacy.

chapters.title: What Voss Wants
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Voss, cornered by his employer's impatience, reveals in soliloquy that he was a Kestrian child shipped to the conquerors' schools—erasure made into a man. He wants the chest burned not for money anymore but because hope hurts. Beat: antagonist humanized, threat deepened.

chapters.title: Tam's Shortcut
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Tam leads them onto a glacier shortcut to make up lost time. The ice groans. Edmund overrides Tam's route at the last fork, saving them from a crevasse field, and Tam's resentment curdles into respect. Beat: humility and hard-earned trust on the ice.

chapters.title: The Crevasse
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Maret falls into a crevasse; Edmund descends on a rope into the blue dark and pulls her out as the lip crumbles. That night Maret calls him 'Uncle' for the first time. Beat: the found family crystallizes in mortal danger.

chapters.title: Halfway Mark
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. At the range's mid refuge, Ilse decrypts her father's final letter hidden in the map's margin: he was the informant, coerced to save Edmund's pregnant mother. Edmund reads it alone and says nothing. Beat: devastating midpoint reversal—the truth he sought is worse than the lie.

chapters.title: Silence on the Scree
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Edmund withdraws, leading mechanically, planning to hand the chest over and vanish at the pass. Maret confronts him: 'You don't get to be a mile again.' Beat: rock bottom; the theme of belonging stated plainly and rejected.

chapters.title: Doss's Confession
chapters.summary: Doss's POV. Doss admits he was the one who sold Edmund's route to the blacklisters twelve years ago, the original sin of Edmund's exile. He offers to leave. Edmund, hollowed by his father's truth, finds he cannot condemn him. Beat: forgiveness given before it's deserved—grace as turning point.

chapters.title: The Storm Decides
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. The early storm hits. They shelter beneath an overhang for two days, sharing food, stories, and the locket. Edmund finally tells Ilse about his father's letter. She says the chest was never about blood—it's about the people who carried it. Beat: acceptance; Edmund chooses the party over the plan.

chapters.title: Ambush at the Col
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Voss's remaining men take the high col and send an avalanche across the party's route. Tam is buried to the chest; Doss digs him out with bare hands. The party is funneled toward Voss's killing ground. Beat: tactical despair; the mountain itself weaponized.

chapters.title: Parley in the Snow
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Edmund walks unarmed into Voss's camp and offers him the truth: the chest can restore Voss's name too—he is on its registry of stolen children. Voss wavers, then his lieutenant fires, wounding Edmund. Beat: mercy offered and betrayed; the wound that will slow the final climb.

chapters.title: Flight Above the Clouds
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Ilse leads the wounded Edmund and the party up a route only she knows from her father's maps, above the cloud deck where Voss can't track them. Edmund, feverish, navigates by memory of his father's descriptions. Beat: the heir and the archivist becoming equals; tenderness under extremity.

chapters.title: The Fever Night
chapters.summary: Maret's POV. Edmund raves with fever, reliving his blacklisting. Maret and Doss keep him alive through the night with melted snow and stubborn talk. Ilse sits with the chest between her knees like a sleeping child. Beat: vulnerability; the cared-for becomes the cared-for.

chapters.title: Voss's Reckoning
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Voss reads the registry page his lieutenant stole and finds his own mother's name. He orders the lieutenant confined and turns the hunt into a private errand. Beat: the antagonist's conversion begins—not redemption yet, but the door open.

chapters.title: The Stair of Winds
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV, recovering. The final ascent: a knife-edge arête called the Stair of Winds, passable only before the snows. Edmund, half-healed, leads them into the wind with the chest lashed to Doss's back. Beat: awe and terror; the mountain at its most sublime.

chapters.title: The Lieutenant's Choice
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. The confined lieutenant escapes and races to destroy the chest at the pass, believing Voss has gone soft. Voss pursues his own man. Beat: antagonist now racing to protect what he came to burn; loyalties inverted.

chapters.title: Summit Storm
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. At the pass, the lieutenant attacks; Edmund, wounded and freezing, fights him hand to hand on the knife-edge. Voss arrives and pulls the lieutenant back from the drop—choosing Kestria's future over his orders. Beat: climax of action; the chest saved by the enemy's own hand.

chapters.title: The First Snow
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. As the tribunal's deadline passes and snow closes the pass behind them, the party is trapped on the far side—safe, but unable to descend to the lowlands where the tribunal sits. Ilse despairs; Edmund laughs for the first time in the book. Beat: apparent defeat that is actually liberation.

chapters.title: The High Kestrians
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Tam leads them to a hidden high valley where three hundred Kestrian descendants have lived unregistered for forty years. The chest's registry includes every one of them. Beat: the inheritance was never one man's—it was everyone's, waiting.

chapters.title: Winter of Testimony
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Snowbound for the winter, the valley records testimony: names, songs, births, losses. Maret learns the script; Doss builds a schoolhouse; Edmund maps the valley in his father's style. Beat: the long warm middle of belonging—identity rebuilt communally.

chapters.title: Voss Among Them
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Voss, exiled by his employer, arrives at the valley's edge and is brought in half-frozen. The people he hunted feed him. He gives testimony about the annexation's records, arming the tribunal case. Beat: the antagonist kneeling into the found family; uneasy, earned.

chapters.title: The Tribunal Letter
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Spring melt opens a courier route; Ilse sends the certified registry to the tribunal. Weeks of waiting. Edmund tends the graves of the valley's dead and finally weeps for his father—informant, coward, and man who tried to save his son. Beat: grief completed; forgiveness of the dead.

chapters.title: Recognition
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. The tribunal rules: Kestrians restored to legal existence, the land empire's annexed titles void. A delegation climbs to the valley with documents and flags. Ilse is named chief archivist of the restored registry. Beat: triumph without trumpets; the chest's promise kept.

chapters.title: The Offer
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. The new government offers Edmund his father's post: Royal Cartographer, and a pardon that would erase his blacklist. He walks alone to the summit pass with the locket, says goodbye to the miles, and comes back down. Beat: the choice made—not the past restored, but a future accepted.

chapters.title: Miles and Years
chapters.summary: Maret's POV, years later. Maret, now the valley's schoolteacher, watches Edmund teach children to read contour lines, Ilse arguing happily with Voss over the archive, Doss ferrying pilgrims on the new trail. Beat: the found family grown roots; inheritance passed forward.

chapters.title: Trail and Summit
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Edmund leads one last climb—the party, older, to the pass where it all turned—carrying a new chest: the valley's own archive, to be placed in the rebuilt capital. At the summit he stops measuring. 'We're not going anywhere,' he says. 'We're already here.' Beat: resolution; belonging as destination and home.
